I've been working this land for 35 years. My body knows the seasons better than any calendar. I'm 59 now, and two of my children work in the city, so I manage most of this myself with my husband. We rely on the well for water — that's what keeps us going through the dry springs.

My 13.1 mu does wheat in winter and maize in summer. That's what my parents did, that's what works here in Quzhou. I rotate them on the same land every year — all 13.1 mu goes to wheat, then all 13.1 mu goes to maize. I don't play around with that system.

For **wheat**: I'll buy the improved certified seed from the township seed station like every year — the traditional stuff doesn't yield as well anymore. I'll do rotary tillage before planting in October, it's what my tiller does best. For fertilizer, I spread the base compound fertilizer before planting, then I go back and top-dress urea at jointing in March. I'll irrigate three times: once before sowing to get the soil right, once at jointing, once at heading. Two pesticide passes — one herbicide early on, one for rust and aphids around heading. I expect around 450 jin per mu, maybe a bit more if spring rains cooperate.

For **maize**: Right after wheat harvest in June, we go straight in with the no-till planter — saves time and my back. Hybrid seed, the kind the village sells in bulk,郑单 or similar. I apply fertilizer at planting and again when it's knee-high. Summer rains help but I'll irrigate twice — once if the seedlings struggle to emerge, once at tasseling if it's dry. Two pesticide rounds — one for cutworm early, one for armyworm if needed. I expect around 550 jin per mu.

With the children sending some money home, I don't need to squeeze every jin out of the land, but I still want a decent harvest. I won't change what works.
